*   **Pitfall:** Effectiveness relies on spatial coherence between adjacent rays; deviations from the cached path require fallback to standard traversal [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that effectiveness relies on spatial coherence between adjacent rays and that deviations require fallback to standard traversal. The evidence explicitly mentions that the technique 'exploits inter-ray coherency' using a buffer storing cells from the last ray. It further explains that for rays visiting the same cells, a flag indicates whether an intersection test is needed or not. This implies that if the spatial coherence holds (rays visit the same cells), the optimized path is taken; if there is a deviation (rays do not visit the same cells or the flag indicates an intersection is needed), the system must perform the standard intersection test (fallback). Thus, the evidence supports the mechanism described in the claim.
